topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes the students, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Biological Nature of Cancer and Mutational Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental biology of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and describe the endogenous, inherited, and cellular drivers of mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Carcinogens and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine everyday environmental exposures and evaluate epidemiological evidence showing geographic and lifestyle variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a case study of viral, environmental, and genetic interactions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical, dietary, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to cause specific forms of DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Two-Stage Carcinogenesis Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction and cooperation between mutagenic initiators and non-mutagenic promoters such as chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Host Factors and Developmental Timing in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes how host tissue proliferative status, developmental stage, and hormonal history modulate susceptibility to carcinogen-induced damage.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic signatures, epidemiological approaches, and laboratory assays used to establish and evaluate carcinogenicity.
